newsitem.title: USA: US, Russia to jointly develop fuel cell technology.
newsitem.headline: US, Russia to jointly develop fuel cell technology.

text.p: The United States and Russia will jointly develop fuel cell technology under an agreement signed by U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and Russian Atomic Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov on Tuesday.
The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced the deal, which was signed in Vienna, Austria, during meetings of the International Atomic Energy Agency.

Fuel cells are a highly-efficient, environmentally-friendly and cost-effective power source, DOE said, Originally developed by both countries for their space programmes, fuel cells convert the energy released by oxidation of a fuel directly into electricity. This happens without combustion, reducing the amount of carbon dioxide released.

"This is another milestone in Russian-American cooperation and a concrete step in the Clinton administration's commitment to diversify the world's energy supply with clean, efficient techologies," O'Leary said in a statement.
